_meta.indication: BRIVIACT is indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, multinational double blind, parallel group, placebo controlled, randomized, fixed-dose; 12-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥16 to 70 years with refractory partial-onset seizures
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Partial-onset seizure (POS) frequency per 7 days over the treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Only the 100 mg/day dose reached nominal significance (percent reduction over placebo 11.7 [95% CI 0.7, 21.4]; p=0.037); 50 mg (p=0.261) and 20 mg (p=0.239) were not significant

nct_ctgov.title: Double-blind, Randomized Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Brivaracetam in Adults With Partial Onset Seizures

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, multinational double blind, parallel group, placebo controlled, randomized, fixed-dose; 12-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥16 to 70 years with refractory partial-onset seizures
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Partial-onset seizure (POS) frequency per 7 days over the treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: The 50 mg/day dose was statistically significant (percent reduction over placebo 12.8 [95% CI 1.7, 22.6]; p=0.025); 20 mg (p=0.492) and 5 mg (p=0.885) were not significant

nct_ctgov.title: Double-blind, Randomized Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Brivaracetam in Adults With Partial Onset Seizures

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, multinational double blind, parallel group, placebo controlled, randomized, fixed-dose; concomitant levetiracetam excluded; 12-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥16 to 80 years with refractory partial-onset seizures (concomitant levetiracetam excluded)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Partial-onset seizure (POS) frequency per 28 days over the treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses statistically significant: 100 mg/day percent reduction over placebo 22.8 (95% CI 13.3, 31.2), p<.001; 200 mg/day 23.2 (95% CI 13.8, 31.6), p<.001; 50% responder rates 38.9% and 37.8% vs 21.6% placebo

nct_ctgov.title: Brivaracetam Efficacy and Safety Study in Subjects With Partial Onset Seizures

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and ≥2% more than placebo) at doses ≥50 mg/day: somnolence and sedation (16% vs 8% placebo), dizziness (12% vs 7%), fatigue (9% vs 4%), and nausea/vomiting symptoms (5% vs 3%). Warnings include suicidal behavior and ideation, and neurological adverse reactions.
target_moa: Brivaracetam has a high and selective affinity for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) in the brain, which is considered the primary mechanism for its anticonvulsant activity.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable and the clinical trial design is similar to previously approved products in the class.

description.text: Added monotherapy indication for partial onset seizures in patients 16 years and older with epilepsy

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for the use of BRIVIACT (brivaracetam) as monotherapy for the treatment of partial onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

description.text: Expanded to include pediatric patients 4 years to less than 16 years of age (previously adults 16 and older) for partial-onset seizures

citations.quote: BRIVIACT is indicated for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 4 years of age and older.

description.text: Expanded population to include pediatric patients ages 1 month to <4 years (tablets/oral solution) and 1 month to <16 years (injection)

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications propose the following changes for Briviact (brivaracetam): expanding the patient population to include pediatric patients ages 1 month to less than 4 years for brivaracetam tablets and oral solution, and expanding the patient population to include pediatric patients ages 1 month to less than 16 years for brivaracetam injection.

basis.text: The application was classified as Standard, not Priority.

summary.text: Standard NDA reviewed as a traditional (non-accelerated) approval; not referred to an advisory committee. Approval was based on three adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials, with deferred pediatric studies required as postmarketing requirements under PREA.

citations.quote:
Priority or Standard	Standard
Submit Date(s)	11/24/2014

The applicant has provided substantial evidence of effectiveness for the use of brivaracetam as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years and older with epilepsy. This conclusion is supported by evidence from three adequate and well-controlled studies (studies 1252, 1253, and 1358) that evaluated the use of brivaracetam at various doses.
Your deferred pediatric studies required under section 505B(a) of the FDCA are required postmarketing studies.

requirement.text: 3042-1: A pharmacokinetic analysis to determine a dosing regimen in children from 4 years to less than 16 years of age that provides drug exposure similar to the effective adult exposure.

citations.quote: 3042-1 A pharmacokinetic analysis to determine a dosing regimen in children from 4 years to less than 16 years of age that provides drug exposure that is similar to the exposure that is effective in adult patients with partial onset seizures.

requirement.text: 3042-2: A pharmacokinetic and safety analysis in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age to determine whether the bioavailability of the IV and oral formulations is similar and to determine an acceptable safety margin of the IV formulation.

citations.quote: 3042-2 A pharmacokinetic and safety analysis in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age to determine whether the bioavailability of the intravenous and oral formulations is similar and to determine an acceptable safety margin of the intravenous formulation when administered at doses that are found acceptable for oral administration.

requirement.text: 3042-3: A prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blinded efficacy and safety study of brivaracetam for adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 4 years of age.

citations.quote: 3042-3 A prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blinded, efficacy and safety study of brivaracetam for the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 4 years of age.

requirement.text: 3042-4: Long-term safety study of brivaracetam in the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age; at least 200 patients must be enrolled.

citations.quote: 3042-4 Long-term safety study of brivaracetam in the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age. Routine safety measures should be monitored. Behavioral and cognitive endpoints should be included. A total of at least 200 patients must be enrolled.
